summary: Financial services platform evaluating Redwood Private VPC for high-throughput reranking/embeddings. Primary gating items are customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), strict mTLS in-transit policies, audit log export, and data residency for EU customers.
timeline: 2026-02-18: Intro call (CTO + CISO) - high level requirements; CISO: 'must be BYOK or HSM-backed', asked about key rotation and attestation.

notes: Lead: Samir P. — strong executive buy-in (CTO + CISO). Procurement timeline aggressive; want contract by 2026-06 if POC good.
Primary use: reranking pipelines for low-latency scoring (p99 target ~ 120ms for 512-token rerank requests), embeddings for semantic search at scale (thousands qps burst).

- In-transit: customer requires mTLS for all control-plane and data-plane connections; mutual auth to customer internal CA preferred. Team asked whether Redwood supports presenting client certs at API ingress and mutual TLS to model workers.

- At-rest: full disk encryption on worker instances + layered envelope encryption for persisted KV/cache and model artifacts. Customer wants assurance that plaintext model weights are never written to persistent storage unencrypted.

- KMS/BYOK: must support AWS KMS (CMEK), GCP CMEK, and on-prem HSM (PKCS#11/EKM) for key wrapping. Customer requested sample IAM/KMS policies and an operational runbook for key rotation and revocation.

- Key rotation: security team mandates quarterly rotation for DEK and annual rotation for KEK with emergency rotation path. Asked how Redwood surfaces rotation events and re-encrypts cached prefixes/KV stores without downtime.

- Secrets management: prefer HashiCorp Vault integration; require Redwood to store only references (secret refs) and support dynamic credential injection at pod start. Asked about rotation hooks and chown/chmod options on temp files.

- Audit logging: must stream audit events (authz decisions, KMS operations, admin actions) to customer SIEM (Splunk) via TLS syslog or Fluentd connector. Retention policy requested: 7 years for transaction logs, 1 year for high-volume debug logs.

- Data residency: production tenant must be pinned to us-east-2 for NA payments data and eu-west-1 for EU clients; logs for EU tenant must remain in region and be delivered to customer's SIEM in eu-west-1.

POC notes: initial deployment used Redwood Private with VPC peering model; validated mTLS handshake to control-plane, tested KMS integration using a test AWS CMK with key policy limited to test IAM role. Observed additional work to automate DEK rollover without cache misses.
Quote from CISO: 'No compromise on keys — if we can't rotate or attest, we can't sign off.'
Requested deliverables: KMS BYOK design doc, example KMS policies, mTLS cert chain diagram, audit event mapping (fields + retention), and sample legal language for DPA/security addendum.

Risk notes: integration requires updates to their change control and on-call runbooks; pen test window to be scheduled in Q2 which may delay go-live. Legal requested changes to data residency and subprocessing list.
Next technical deep-dive with security engineering (Janelle leading) — target: 2026-03-22. SE to bring KMS integration checklist and a demo of key rotation workflow.
